sentences.text: Sthenarosaurus is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid found in the Toarcian-aged Main Alum Shale in Whitby, England. The holotype of Sthenarosaurus consists of an incomplete skeleton lacking a skull. Sthenarosaurus is assumed to have been a small plesiosaur reaching up to 3 meters in length when fully grown.
This animal possessed short, thick coracoids and a broad, strong pelvis. The dorsal vertebrae of Sthenarosaurus had short but very broad and high centers with thick neural spines.
The species Sthenarosaurus dawkinsi was named and described in 1909 by D. M. S. Watson. The type specimen for Sthenarosaurus dawkinsi is a set of postcrania discovered in Whitby.

Sthenarosaurus has been classified within Pliosauroidea in the order Plesiosauria since its description in 1909. Sthenarosaurus was considered the sister taxon to Archaeonectrus based on similarities in shoulder blade, coracoid, and cervical vertebrae shapes.
Researchers suggest that Sthenarosaurus might represent an unknown clade of plesiosaurs.
Sthenarosaurus lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
